comment: Text copied out of a terminal (D-371). Claude Code lays out its text by the width of the terminal itself, the rows after the first indented by two spaces, so a copied paragraph breaks in the middle of a sentence. A row is joined to the next with a space when the first word of the next would not have fit on it (its length on the screen, a space and that word are more than the width); the indent the following rows share goes. Empty lines, points of a list, lines of a table or a box and lines indented deeper (code) keep their breaks. Lines are given with \n and come back with \n. The first row of a selection usually starts after the mark of a message, so it counts as wide as its text and the indent of the rows after it.

rows.name: a paragraph of Claude Code at 80 columns
rows.text:
Tip: You can control how big a workflow is just by prompting. Ask for a
     small workflow, cap it with "use at most 5 agents", or set the default with
     Dynamic workflow size in /config.
rows.copied: Tip: You can control how big a workflow is just by prompting. Ask for a small workflow, cap it with "use at most 5 agents", or set the default with Dynamic workflow size in /config.

rows.name: two paragraphs keep the empty line between them
rows.text:
The first paragraph is long enough that
  it wraps here.

  The second one is short.
rows.copied:
The first paragraph is long enough that it wraps here.

The second one is short.

  Next I run the tests.
